items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: Then later, in '47, this was Charlie Parker, 'Dark Shadows,' 'Bird's Nest,' 'This is Always,' 'Cool Blues'. Earl Coleman sang on 'Dark Shadows' and 'This is Always.'

ctx.x: And Jazz at the Philharmonic. 'How High The Moon.' That was Paul Leslie, whose real name was Les Paul. He turned it around because of contractual agreements with some other company.
Then later, in '47, this was Charlie Parker, 'Dark Shadows,' 'Bird's Nest,' 'This is Always,' 'Cool Blues'. Earl Coleman sang on 'Dark Shadows' and 'This is Always.'
Then I see my own thing here on Black-and-White. 'Red Boogie' and 'By The River St. Marie.' That's when our group sang. I guess we were copying Nat Cole's style.
